A rant about a classic Chinese novel:

The classic tale is the most repeatedly adapted story in Chinese cinema to the point of becoming annoying and boring. Every year or two, some major production will release ANOTHER film featuring the main character, and each film is the same recycled content that you’ve seen before. One film might focus on battling deities, another might include a famous warrior, and yet another could feature a dragon or a celestial being, repeating the cycle. The last time I saw anything creative in these adaptations was probably from a well-known filmmaker about 20 years ago. It just feels like each new film is just "Main Character: Now with more overdone CGI and a different lead actor." A good comparison would be the blockbuster action series; seriously, why do people still watch that?

The side effect of the popularity of the main character is that the only thing game developers seem to think of when they want to incorporate Chinese elements into their games is: Add the main character. Oh, you want Chinese weapons? Don’t worry, here’s a magical staff. It wouldn’t be that bad if they bothered to include more Chinese elements after the main character, but usually, he is their "token Chinese element to show off how culturally diverse our game is." An exception is a game based on deities, as they naturally include more Chinese elements.

Now, I definitely agree that the classic tale is a fantastic fit for an adventure, with all the monsters and different locations traveled making it incredible and showcasing the best themes from Chinese mythology. However, selfishly, as someone who is super tired of seeing the main character everywhere whenever a game integrates Chinese elements, I hope that if a certain game developer ever makes another adventure like this, they will either use another mythology or another Chinese story. Perhaps when they include a legendary snake character, they could create something unique, or explore themes related to the Jade Emperor, etc.
